PLAINTIFE’S SUPPLEMENT TO MOTION FOR TARGETED VACATUR OF ECF
NOS. 64 AND 84, WITHDRAWAL OR MODIFICATION OF THE MAGISTRATE-

JUDGE REFERRAL, AND RELATED INTERIM RELIEF (ECF NO. 93)

Plaintiff submits this Supplement, upon leave of Court, to update ECF No. 93 for
developments on the docket after its filing. It adds no ground and requests no new relief.

I. SUBSEQUENT DEVELOPMENTS

1. On October 22, 2026, an unnumbered docket entry stated: “Case Reassigned to
Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick. Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis no longer assigned to
the case.”

2. On October 22, 2026, ECF No. 96, signed by Magistrate Judge Davis, denied
ECF No. 86 as moot. Its docket entry states: “The case has been reassigned to Magistrate Judge
William E. Fitzpatrick.”

3. ECF No. 96 identifies ECF No. 86 only. It records no determination on the

matters identified in ECF No. 86, Part V. It does not refer to ECF No. 93.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF Document 99-1 Filed 10/23/26 Page 3 of 6 PagelD#
1024

4, Plaintiff’s Rule 72(a) Objections to ECF No. 96, filed with this Supplement,
request determination of the authority under which ECF No. 96 was issued and identification of
the procedure by which the successor designation was made.

IL. EFFECT ON THE RELIEF REQUESTED IN ECF NO. 93 { 10

5. (R1) Referral. The removal of Magistrate Judge Davis from the assignment is
accomplished. Plaintiff does not seek his reinstatement. The remaining referral question concerns
the authorized disposition of the referred matters and any warranted correction of the successor
designation, as requested in the Objections to ECF No. 96. Plaintiff maintains (R1) to that extent.

6. (R2) Vacatur. ECF No. 96 grants no relief from ECF No. 64 or ECF No. 84. Plaintiff
maintains (R2).

7. (R3) Restoration and preservation. ECF No. 96 grants no relief as to ECF Nos. 15,
54, or 59. Plaintiff maintains (R3).

8. (R4) Affirmative adjudication. ECF No. 96 grants no relief as to the merits of ECF
Nos. 15, 54, or 59. Plaintiff maintains (R4).

9. (R5) Interim protection. The component in (R5)(a) directed to further substantive
action by Magistrate Judge Davis is addressed by the reassignment. Plaintiff maintains (R5)(b),
concerning reliance on the nonproduction condition in ECF No. 64, and (R5)(c), concerning the
sequencing of the amendment and financial-conflict issues relative to any claim-terminating
disposition of ECF Nos. 10, 21, or 45.

10. (R6) Existing objections. Plaintiff requests that the October 22 developments be
addressed within the coordinated determination requested in (R6), with the prospective disposition
in ECF No. 96 kept distinct from the retrospective requests in ECF No. 93.

11. (R7) Decision record. Plaintiff maintains (R7) to the extent the findings and reasons

requested are necessary to decide the relief still sought.
